snippet.title: Ese hueco alrededor del tronco en una casa del árbol NO está de adorno
snippet.description:
🌳 Ese hueco alrededor del tronco en una casa del árbol no está de adorno: el árbol sigue creciendo, y sin él el tronco levanta el piso hasta romperlo.
Construimos una casa del árbol desde cero, problema por problema: tirafondo → tornapuntas → barandal → balaustres → techo de dos aguas → perno de anclaje → la holgura.
Y si en tu casa hay un tendedero o una hamaca amarrados con alambre a un árbol, cámbialo por una cinta ancha y floja.
¿Tú tuviste una casa del árbol? 👇
📚 Fuentes
• Treehouse Supplies. Treehouse Attachment Bolts (TABs) FAQ.
• The Treehouse Guide. Single tree; Knee braces.
• International Code Council (2021). International Residential Code, R312 (barandales).
• Michigan State University Extension. Girdling wires and ropes.

Neste segundo episódio, temos uma prova INÉDITA: NADA ALÉM DE UM GLOSS! Porque toda blogueira de sucesso precisa de um bom gloss para começar sua carreira, né, more? E pelo visto a Corrida também resolveu entrar no mundo do empreendedorismo! 💄

snippet.title: Finally an accessible museum
snippet.description: A museum all about the history of blindness! Not to mention it was fully accessible to the blind!! It was truly an honor and amazing experience getting to explore The DOT Experience created by American Printing House for the Blind where accessibility was not an afterthought, but actually thought about in the original design. I felt totally free being able to learn and feel everything. There was braille, QR codes that you can scan to listen to audio or large print for those who have trouble seeing, but can still read. Even the second my daughter saw it she got so excited to see all the Braille for me. Not to mention there were no touchscreens, and everything was in a layout that you could navigate on your own. It was very thought out from the moment you entered with an orientation station that was all Braille and tactile, as well as the layout of all the exhibits. Getting to be the tour guide for my family instead of having to wait for everything to be described to me and just trying to imagine everything was truly freedom. I seriously hope other museums can get ideas from this and make it an accessible experience for everyone. This is the true meaning of access for everyone and just because something is for the Blind does not mean it is not helpful for others. One love.

snippet.title: When Life Throws a Curveball, True Support Reveals Itself 👇
snippet.description:
When Life Throws a Curveball, True Support Reveals Itself 👇

Late to their dinner, he shows up with a secret — a new puppy hidden away from the shelter.

The warm gesture breaks the ice, but then comes the bombshell.

She’s unexpectedly pregnant.

His calm assurance is everything she needs.

Not panic.

Not judgment.

Just steady support and a promise that whatever happens next, he’s in it with her.

In the heat of uncertainty, love isn’t about grand gestures — it’s about showing up.

👉 Real love listens before reacting, no matter how surprising the news.

👉 Life’s hardest moments demand partnership, not pressure.

👉 Courage is asking for help and finding the strength to move forward together.

The uncomfortable truth?

Life often surprises us when we’re least prepared.

Plans change overnight.

And the people who truly matter aren’t those who run from the challenge — but those who stand by your side anyway.

So the real question is:

How do we show up when someone’s world is shifting beneath their feet? 👇💬

snippet.title: Canadians awarded $56 million in defamation case against alleged cult leader
snippet.description:
In part one of this five-part W5 investigation: “Fake Filtered Cult Leader,” CTV News’ investigative unit examines a self-described spiritual teacher whose online presence helped attract followers around the world. Drawing on interviews and extensive reporting, W5 explores concerns raised by former members and the questions surrounding the organization behind the carefully curated public image.

A Hawaii jury has handed three Canadians one of the largest civil awards in the state’s history after a yearslong battle with an alleged cult leader.

The jury ordered Liane Wilson, who goes by Liana Shanti online, to pay Paula Haygarth and Byron and Stefanie Horvath, all from Saskatchewan, US$40.1 million, or just over C$56 million.

snippet.title: Henry Nowak's family tell us they think his death was politicised
snippet.description:
Henry Nowak’s family has accused some politicians of playing a "political game" with their son’s murder.

Speaking to ITV News UK Editor Paul Brand, the family said they had "worked hard" to keep politics out of Henry’s story - and that he "would have hated" the rioting in response to his death.

Police bodycam footage showing officers arresting Henry as he lay dying was released after the sentencing of his killer, 23-year-old Vickrum Digwa, and sparked global condemnation.

The following day, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage delivered an emergency address, calling for the public to respond with "pure cold rage" and demanding an end to what he described as "two-tier policing".

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch criticised Farage's comments, but said race should not be used "as a way of defining laws". 

Then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer denied the existence of two-tier policing and accused others of seeking to exploit the Nowaks' tragedy - after Henry's father had told the public: “We do not want his death to be used to create further division, hatred or tension." 

Protests soon erupted in Southampton, with violent disorder resulting in 12 police officers being injured.

Now, in a special ITV Tonight documentary, Henry’s family have condemned the riots and called for an end to the political division.

Henry's mother, Lucy Ross, said she believed people had repeatedly tried to use her son's death to advance wider political arguments.

"I suppose that's the game they play, and I can't do anything about that. But when they think it all links together - no, it doesn't."

"Olivia's lost her brother, and I've lost my son. I'm not interested in your political game," she added.

On whether she felt 'two-tier policing' was a factor in Henry's death, Lucy Ross said she did not want to make a broader political point but had questions about Henry’s specific case.

"I'll put it this way. I want to know why Henry was on the floor, and he got treated the way he did, but that family got treated [in] a different way. What is that?"

Henry's father, Mark Nowak, told ITV News his son "was not a divisive person" and the political response to his murder "didn't sit with Henry's values or our values".

Henry's stepmother, Katie Nowak, added: "We understand why people were angry.

"We think everyone should have a right to protest and have their voice heard, but not the riots."
